brief: Goldman Prime Services' weekly US equities rundown covers positioning, macro and cross-asset flows for September 11-18, 2026. The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% as expected, but the dot plot turned more hawkish, showing one more 2026 hike and no 2027 cut; only 2 of 26 participants saw just the September hike for the year. GIR still expects an October hike, a 3.25%-3.5% neutral rate, and a cut path into 2027-2028. Separately, Anthropic's "Dario Doomsday" call for slower frontier AI progress triggered a sharp rotation out of AI and momentum names early in the week, spiking the desk's Vol Panic Index to its largest one-day decline in 10 years before Thursday's rally reversed it. Prime flow was net risk-on: the largest net buying in five weeks, led by short covers in macro products and long buys in software, while health care was sold for a fifth straight week. In commodities, Brent positioning swung from bullish (Houthi/Saudi pipeline risk) to partial liquidation once Saudi Arabia signaled it would restore pipeline capacity, while gold corrected on the hike before the desk moved to rebuild length.
